scope: Diagnosis and first-line treatment of de Quervain tenosynovitis.

keyRecommendations.text: It is a stenosing overuse condition of the first extensor compartment, affecting extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus.
Pain and tenderness over and proximal to the radial styloid are the clinical picture, and diagnosis is predominantly clinical.
The review found benefit from adding thumb-spica immobilisation to a local corticosteroid injection, and greater pain reduction when the injection was ultrasound-guided.
keyRecommendations.population: Patients treated for de Quervain tenosynovitis

clinicalBottomLine: Diagnose de Quervain tenosynovitis clinically from radial-styloid pain in the first extensor compartment. The review's synthesis supports a local corticosteroid injection plus thumb-spica immobilisation, with ultrasound guidance associated with greater pain reduction.
notableCaveats: The review says inflammation remains controversial and that overuse degeneration is the more likely mechanism. It does not present the Finkelstein test as a stand-alone diagnostic criterion.
